questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Because of the uncertainty caused by covid-19, it felt easier to be in a Nordic country (more likely the exchange would actually take place). I also thought it was nice to be in a big city because of the cultural activities etc. (for instance also when you do not know so many people). Finland seemed more exotic than the Scandinavian countries and at the same time, the university offered many interesting courses and was ok ranked.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was provided on the website and send directly to me by e-mail. The echange coordinators were very helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The first week was filled with introductions. Tutors (other students) were very helpful and even offered to go to immigration authorities etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was just next to the campus and mainly for the faculty of agriculture and forestry. It was mentioned online and was easy to find. I also got something offered through the university.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived in a shared apartment, and the only Finninsh people I got to know were my flatmates, so I highly recommend it, if you want to know more Finnish people.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have to apply both there and at KU. You need to provide a learning agreement before the course plan is available and need special forms for each step. I highly recommend an excel-sheet with course codes and course names, both for first and second priority courses (in case the final course offer differs from previous years).

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The exchange coordinators at Helsinki University were very helpful to answer on e-mail.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: The IT system was brand new and there was some technical issues, but I e-mail study support and they then enrolled me manually

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do not stress. The professors and the support team will help (just write them by e-mail) and you can even be enrolled later. Another good thing to know is that you can register for more courses than you need, go to the first lecture, and then unenroll yourself. You can even just decide not to show up, because only courses you pass are registered.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some master courses were recommended on first year of the master or last year of the BA. Those courses were generally too easy.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Less hours with exercises/calculations, mainly just lectures. Quite many courses contain homework/assignments. In some of my courses they contribute to the final grade and in others not. In some courses, there are no traditional exams, instead you have to fill in a learning diary.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Field crop quality, basic biotechnology applications in forestry, breeding of crops, plant biochemistry and cell biology, wood science, environmental technology in agriculture - theoretical bases, responsible business management in the global bioeconomy, BLUP and variance components

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Wood science was really good with hands on and it is something you cannot get in Denmark (perhaps not very relevant in a Danish context, but fun)
Breeding of crops was nice, because they breed more crops (including apple and strawberry) for winter hardiness than we do in Denmark

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I spent more on activities and trips than expected.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Candy is cheap - and you can go to Tallinn and buy alcohol like the Finns

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are lots of student unions with different themes. Most of them in Finnish, but some in English and in Swedish.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I joined a Swedish speaking student group. It was a nice way to meet some Finnish people and not only international students. I will also recommend going to sitsits. It is an event, normally on a weekday, where the student unions eat dinner, sing lots of songs and drink snaps.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: It is nice to go to Porvoo, Soumenlinna, Sipoonkorpi and Nuuksio. If you have more days off, it is nice to rent a cottage (on air bnb eg) and a car with some friends. I went to the area around Savonlinna with some other Danes. You can go to national parks and at night in sauna - and most often there is a lake nearby.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It is quite similar to the Danish culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join some student groups and go to sitsits. There is a table plan and so many songs that you can go even if you do not know anybody.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The Finns do not nod or smile on the street - or even in national parks. They are friendly when they finally start speaking.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Sauna

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Join student groups, know that you can drop courses if you find them boring and enjoy the nature

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask the student help - they answer fast and are willing to help

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To meet people from all over Europe and just to spent some time in new surroundings after a year in lockdown at home

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To get to know Finnish people

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
